"""Run the class-code-assistant first pass on one employer, several, or all of them.

Examples (from the repository root):

    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --all
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer <employer-slug>
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --local path/to/sources --employer <employer-slug>
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet <employer-slug>
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from cca import records, render  # noqa: E402
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402
from cca.rules import WorksheetError, allocate  # noqa: E402
from fetch_sources import fetch  # noqa: E402

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REFS = SKILL_DIR / "references"


def load_sources(args):
    sources = json.loads((REFS / "sources.json").read_text())
    root = Path(args.local) if args.local else Path(args.cache)
    if not args.local:
        fetch(root, sources, None if args.all else args.employer)
    manifest_path = root / "manifest.json"
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text()) if manifest_path.exists() else {"fetched_at": "local copy", "files": {}}
    guide_path = root / "classification-guide.md"
    if not guide_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"error: no classification guide at {guide_path}; the authoritative rules are required")
    guide_bytes = guide_path.read_bytes()
    run = {
        "fetched_at": manifest["fetched_at"],
        "guide_sha256": hashlib.sha256(guide_bytes).hexdigest(),
        "guide_source": sources["classification_guide"] if not args.local else str(guide_path),
        "employer_source": sources["employer_files"] if not args.local else str(root / "employers"),
    }
    return root, Guide(guide_bytes.decode("utf-8")), run


def init_worksheet(rec, path):
    """Scaffold a worksheet listing every judgment the analyst must make for this employer, with nothing filled in."""
    ws = {
        "employer": rec["employer_name"],
        "employees": {e["id"]: {"name": e["name"], "position": e["position"], "duty_code": None,
                                "basis": "TODO: the employee's actual duties and the record that shows them",
                                "records": []} for e in rec["register"]},
        "owners": {},
        "work_type_codes": {t: None for t in sorted({r["work_type"] for r in rec["timesheets"]})},
        "site_codes": {s: None for s in sorted({r["site"] for r in rec["signins"] if r["employee_id"]})},
        "route_code": None,
        "subcontract_work_codes": {w: None for w in sorted({r["work"] for r in rec["sub_payments"]})},
        "subcontractor_certificate_matches": {},
        "facts": [],
        "confirmations": [],
        "open_items": [],
        "unused_records": {},
    }
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"error: {path} already exists; not overwriting it")
    path.write_text(json.dumps(ws, indent=2) + "\n")


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Class code and payroll allocation first pass (Linden Shore Mutual).")
    who = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    who.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="every employer folder at the source location")
    who.add_argument("--employer", action="append", help="employer folder slug (repeatable)")
    who.add_argument("--init-worksheet", metavar="SLUG", help="scaffold deliverables/worksheets/SLUG.json and stop")
    ap.add_argument("--local", help="read a local copy (classification-guide.md + employers/<slug>/) instead of fetching")
    ap.add_argument("--cache", default=".cache/sources", help="where fetched sources are written (default .cache/sources)")
    ap.add_argument("--worksheets", default="deliverables/worksheets", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="deliverables", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.init_worksheet:
        args.employer = [args.init_worksheet]

    root, guide, run = load_sources(args)
    slugs = sorted(p.name for p in (root / "employers").iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if args.all else args.employer
    hp = json.loads((REFS / "house_practice.json").read_text())

    if args.init_worksheet:
        path = args.worksheets / f"{args.init_worksheet}.json"
        init_worksheet(records.load(root / "employers" / args.init_worksheet), path)
        print(f"wrote {path}: fill in every null and TODO from the employer's records, then run --employer {args.init_worksheet}")
        return 0

    results = []
    for slug in slugs:
        ws_path = args.worksheets / f"{slug}.json"
        if not ws_path.exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"error: no worksheet for {slug} at {ws_path}. Run --init-worksheet {slug}, then fill it "
                             f"in from the records (see SKILL.md, step 3).")
        try:
            result = allocate(guide, hp, records.load(root / "employers" / slug), json.loads(ws_path.read_text()))
        except (records.RecordError, WorksheetError) as exc:
            raise SystemExit(f"error: {slug}: {exc}")
        render.write_codes_csv(args.out / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv", result, guide)
        results.append(result)
        print(f"{slug}: " + ", ".join(f"{c} {v:.2f}" for c, v in result.totals.items())
              + f" | adjustments {len(result.adjustments)}, open items {len(result.open_items)}, "
                f"questions {len(result.questions)}, employer split {'accepted' if result.accepts_employer_split else 'not accepted'}")

    if args.all:
        report_path, questions_path = args.out / "audit-report.md", args.out / "audit-questions.md"
    else:
        report_path = args.out / "runs" / f"{'+'.join(slugs)}-audit-report.md"
        questions_path = args.out / "runs" / f"{'+'.join(slugs)}-audit-questions.md"
    report_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report_path.write_text(render.report(results, guide, run))
    questions_path.write_text(render.questions(results))
    (args.out / "run-manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        **run, "employers": {r.rec["file"].slug: {k: f"{v:.2f}" for k, v in r.totals.items()} for r in results},
        "report": str(report_path), "questions": str(questions_path)}, indent=2) + "\n") if args.all else None
    print(f"wrote {report_path} and {questions_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Check the deliverables against the assignment's format rules. Exit status 1 on any failure.

Checks: the six codes CSVs (exact header, cents, no zero rows, rationale_ref as printed in the guide); CSV totals match
the report's allocation tables; one report and one question section per employer; every adjustment in the report is
named in that employer's questions; no employer names or IDs are hard-coded in the Skill's code; interview exports
are unchanged since they were committed.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402

HEADER = ["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]
CENTS = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d{2}$")


def sections(text):
    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", text, flags=re.M)
    return {parts[i].strip(): parts[i + 1] for i in range(1, len(parts), 2)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="deliverables", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--guide", default=".cache/sources/classification-guide.md", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--employers", default=".cache/sources/employers", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    failures, checks = [], 0

    def check(ok, message):
        nonlocal checks
        checks += 1
        if not ok:
            failures.append(message)

    guide = Guide(args.guide.read_text())
    slugs = sorted(p.name for p in args.employers.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
    report = (args.out / "audit-report.md").read_text()
    questions = (args.out / "audit-questions.md").read_text()
    rep_sections, q_sections = sections(report), sections(questions)
    names = {}

    for slug in slugs:
        app = (args.employers / slug / "application.md").read_text()
        name = re.search(r"^#\s*([^:\n]+)", app, re.M).group(1).strip()
        names[slug] = name
        path = args.out / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv"
        check(path.exists(), f"{path} is missing")
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        with open(path, newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))

content.content:
# Premium audit first pass: class codes and payroll allocation

Prepared by the class-code-assistant Skill as a **first pass for review by Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor**. It is not audit work until she has reviewed it (house practice HP-11). It classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium.

- Classification rules: Linden Shore Mutual classification guide excerpt, edition of July 2025, sha256 `89480f691737`, read from https://drive.google.com/file/d/REDACTED/view.
- Employer files read from https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED at 2026-10-27T02:22:51+00:00.
- Three kinds of statement are kept apart:
  - **Confirmed rules** (`HP-n`) are what Nadia Brennan stated in interviews 1 and 2, listed with timestamps in `skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md`, together with the guide (`CG-nn`).
  - **Facts** cite the employer record they come from.
  - **Open items** are unresolved judgements. Each one gives the proposed handling, why, and the Skill's reading (`R-n`) where one was needed. Each is on the employer's question list for confirmation, and Nadia reviews the proposal (HP-10).
- **Questionable records** are used as written and sent to the employer to confirm (HP-15).

## Which two employers to call first

Nadia left the choice to the analyst, with reasons (HP-12). The order ranks employers by the payroll the first pass places in a code above what the employer reported there: payroll moved in from another code, plus payroll added. It is in dollars of payroll, not premium. A larger figure means the employer's own split, and so the figures underwriting would otherwise quote from, is further from the records. Ties go to the employer with more open items.

# Employer worksheet (`deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`)

The worksheet holds the judgments that need a reader: what each person actually does, and which guide code describes a
type of work. The engine does everything else from the records: the thresholds, splits, flat amounts, caps,
subcontractor shares and comparison with the employer. Start from `run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`.

Every code must be one the guide describes. Every judgment cites the record it rests on. If a record does not settle a
judgment, make the best-supported proposal and add an `open_items` entry; do not leave it implied.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `employees.<id>.duty_code` | The code describing the person's **actual** duties from the file (HP-1). For crew with timesheets, give the expected code; the timesheets then decide. For office staff, give `C-110`; the sign-in log then applies the five-day test. |
| `employees.<id>.basis` | One or two sentences: what the person does, the record and date that show it, and the guide paragraph. Say so when the only evidence is a job title. |
| `employees.<id>.records` | Files the basis rests on. The payroll register is added automatically. |
| `employees.<id>.field_code` | Optional. Overrides the site-based code for a clerical person who meets the job-site threshold. |
| `owners.<id or name>` | `included` (no election of exclusion), `field_work`, `field_code`, `basis`, `records`. Excluded owners are listed for the record only. |
| `work_type_codes` | Timesheet `work_type` to code. |
| `site_codes` | Sign-in `site` to code; `null` when no code in the guide describes the work there. |
| `route_code` | Code for route ride-along weeks, when a route log exists. |
| `subcontract_work_codes` | Subcontracted `work` to code. |
| `subcontractor_certificate_matches` | Payee name to certificate name, when they differ. Always raised as an open item. |
| `facts` | `{fact, record}` statements the report lists as documented. |
| `confirmations` | `{about, question}` employer questions for records relied on that the engine does not know about, such as an owner's exclusion election. Name the person or record and the document needed. |
| `open_items` | `{about, proposal, why, records, employer_question?, merge_with?}`. `merge_with` adds context to an item the engine raises for the same person. |
| `unused_records` | File name to the reason it was not used. |

---
name: class-code-assistant
description: First-pass premium audit for Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation new business. It reads an employer's payroll register, application, business description, field notes and time records, then assigns company class codes. It allocates payroll to each code, citing the classification guide paragraph and the supporting records, and drafts employer-specific audit questions. Use it when a premium auditor asks to check, classify or allocate an employer's payroll, or to run the first pass on an employer file. It never sets rates or quotes premium.
---

# Class code assistant

This Skill does the first pass that Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, reviews before underwriting quotes an
employer. It classifies people and allocates payroll. It does **not** set rates, compute premium or quote.

## Ground rules

- **Use only the company's own rules.** The authoritative rules are the Linden Shore Mutual classification guide
  excerpt (paragraphs `CG-nn`), read from the location in `references/sources.json` on every run. Public
  classification manuals, such as NCCI or state manuals, do not apply and give wrong answers. Never use them.
- **Apply house practice as the auditor stated it.** `references/house-practice.md` keeps three lists apart:
  confirmed rules from interviews 1 and 2 (HP-1 to HP-15), stated gaps where the auditor has no rule, and the Skill's
  own readings (R2, R3, R4, R6, R14), which are always raised as open items. The numbers are in `references/house_practice.json`.
- **Classify by actual duties, not titles (HP-1).** The records in the file decide, not the employer's application
  (HP-7).
- **Gray areas: propose, explain and flag, never invent.** When neither the guide nor house practice covers a case,
  propose a treatment, write down why, and add an open item that goes on the employer's question list and
  that the auditor reviews (HP-10). Never present a proposal as company
  rule.
- **Keep facts apart from assumptions.** Every fact cites the employer record it comes from. Every assumption is an
  open item.

## Inputs

Per employer, one folder named by its slug (for example `acme-roofing`) holding:

| File | Required | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `payroll-register.csv` (`employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`, optional `travel_days,travel_allowance_paid`) | yes | wages per person; out-of-town allowance |
| `application.md` (table of code, employees, payroll; employer's note) | yes | the employer's own split, for comparison |
| a `.md` stating `Audit period <Month D, YYYY> to <Month D, YYYY>` (usually `business-description.md`) | yes | audit period filter |
| `field-notes.md`, `business-description.md` | no | duties, owner status, subcontractors |
| `*timesheet*.csv` (`date,employee_id,work_type,hours`) | no | crew work by type, counted in days (HP-2, HP-13, R2) |
| `*sign*in*.csv` (`date,employee_id,site`) | no | clerical job-site days; five or more moves the whole pay to the governing code (HP-4) |
| `route-log.csv` (`date,driver_id,ride_along_id`) + `weekly-payroll.csv` (`week_start,week_end,employee_id,gross_pay`) | no | route split: pay weeks with two or more ride days go to T-610 (HP-2) |
| `subcontractor-payments.csv` (`date,subcontractor,work,invoice,amount_paid`) + `insurance-certificates.csv` (`subcontractor,certificate_no,coverage_from,coverage_to`) | no | uninsured subcontractors; a certificate must cover the whole audit period (HP-5) |

Other files are listed in the report as not used. Give the reason in the worksheet's `unused_records`.

Plus one **worksheet** per employer, `deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`, holding the analyst's judgments (step 3).

## How to run

From the repository root, with Python 3.10 or later and no other dependencies:

1. **Fetch and scaffold.** Run `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`. This
   downloads the guide and employer files into `.cache/sources/` and writes an empty worksheet listing every person,
   work type, subcontracted trade and receipts column that needs a decision.
2. **Read everything.** Read the guide (`.cache/sources/classification-guide.md`) and every file in
   `.cache/sources/employers/<slug>/`. Note which statements are documented, and where the employer's application
   disagrees with its own records.
3. **Fill in the worksheet** following `references/worksheet.md`. For each person, record the code that describes
   what they actually do, a `basis` citing the record, and the `records` relied on. Map each timesheet work type, job
   subcontracted trade to a guide code, and name the off-site catering receipts columns. Record owners,
   documented facts, confirmations to ask the employer for, and open items for gray areas. Do **not** do arithmetic
   here; the engine applies the house rules.
4. **Run.** Use `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer <slug>` for one employer, or `--all`
   for every employer folder at the source. Add `--local <dir>` to use a local copy laid out as
   `<dir>/classification-guide.md` and `<dir>/employers/<slug>/`, instead of fetching.
5. **Check.** Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` and
   `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/validate.py`. Then read the report section and the questions as the
   auditor would, and fix the worksheet, not the outputs, if anything is wrong.
6. **Hand over** to the auditor for review (HP-11). The output is a first pass, not audit work.

## Outputs

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv` | Exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`. One row per code carrying payroll, dollars to the cent, `rationale_ref` = the guide paragraph describing the code |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` (`--all`) or `deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-report.md` | Call-first order with reasons. Per employer: whether the employer's split is accepted and the records that decision rests on, the allocation against the employer's split, where and why they differ, every adjustment with person or payment, amount and records, an employee-by-employee basis, documented facts, open items, and notes on unused records |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` (or `deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-questions.md`) | Per employer, questions naming the person, subcontractor or record, and the document needed. Every adjustment, record relied on, questionable record and open item is covered (HP-9, HP-10, HP-15) |
| `deliverables/run-manifest.json` (`--all`) | Fetch time, guide sha256 and totals per employer, for traceability |

## Error behaviour

The run stops with `error: ...` and a non-zero exit, writing nothing for that employer, when:

- the guide, the payroll register, the application split or the audit period statement is missing or unreadable;
- a CSV lacks a required column;
- the worksheet is missing, does not list exactly the register's employees, leaves a decision unfilled, or names a
  class code the guide does not describe;
- a timesheet work type, a subcontracted trade or the route code has no worksheet mapping. The engine
  will not guess one.

Conditions the records can't settle become open items and do not stop the run: a tie in timesheet days, a
certificate name mismatch, an allowance with no travel days, weekly pay that does not sum to the register, a sign-in on
a fixed holiday (used as written and sent to the employer, HP-15), a five-day threshold met at an employer with no
field code, or a caterer with no receipts record.

## Supporting files

- `references/house-practice.md`: the audit team's unwritten rules from the interview, with timestamps, plus this
  stated gaps and the Skill's readings.
- `references/house_practice.json`: the numeric parameters (flat owner amount, day threshold, subcontractor share,
  allowance cap).
- `references/sources.json`: where the guide and employer files are kept.
- `references/worksheet.md`: the worksheet fields and how to fill them.
- `scripts/fetch_sources.py`: downloads the sources; standard library only, no credentials.
- `scripts/run.py`: the command-line entry point. `scripts/cca/` holds the guide parser, record loader, rule engine
  and renderer.
- `scripts/validate.py`: checks the deliverables against the required formats.

content.text:
I updated the Skill with interview 2, re-ran it on all six employers from the Drive sources, and committed everything; nothing was pushed. The tests pass (14), the validator passes (270 of 270), and every employer's allocation reconciles to the cent. Both interview exports are committed and unchanged.

## Decisions that changed
| Employer | Before | Now | Why (Nadia, interview 2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | Accepted (catering crew under F-720) | **Not accepted:** all 340,725.35 under F-710 | Caterer code needs off-site catering at 40% or more of receipts. The receipts file shows 22.00%. |
| Annapolis Courier | 30,078.05 moved to T-610 | **22,808.75** moved, from Lena Ortiz only | Only pay weeks with two or more ride days move. Lena has 25 such weeks; Paul's two ride days fall in separate weeks, so he stays C-110. |
| Severn Homebuilders | R-310 18,987.39 | **R-310 27,567.39** | A certificate must cover the whole audit period. Kent Island's ends 2026-01-31, so its September payment (8,580.00) is now added too. Tenbury Ridge's covers the whole period, so it's still not added. |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | Same totals | Same totals, firmer basis | Teresa Lindqvist moves to R-310 because it's the field code with the most payroll, not because of site names. Crew codes are counted in days, not hours. |
| Patuxent Electric | Unchanged | Unchanged | Nadia confirmed the flat 63,700.00 applies whatever the owner's actual wages, and the 47.00-a-day allowance cap. |
| Harbor Point Legal | Accepted | Accepted | Tomas Reyes passes the five-day test, but the firm has no field code to move him to. He stays C-110 as an open item. |

Earlier open items that interview 2 settled are now applied as company rules: holiday sign-ins are used as written and sent to the employer. Disagreements between an employer's application and its records now go on that employer's question list instead of being listed as gray areas. In [house-practice.md](skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md), the reference I keep from the two interviews, confirmed rules, gaps Nadia said she has no rule for, and my own interpretations are kept in separate lists.

## Who to call first
1. **Bay Crest Exteriors.** 319,158.10 of payroll sits in a different code from the employer's application, which put 7 of 10 people under clerical while the timesheets show 8 crew members.
2. **Larkspur Lane Bistro.** The whole catering crew (114,293.80) moves from the caterer code to the restaurant code.

Severn Homebuilders is within 2% of Larkspur, and the report says so. Of Severn's figure, 52,260.78 is added only because certificates are missing, so a call there could actually change the numbers before Friday. If Nadia would rather spend the call where it can move the figures, Severn is the better second choice.

## Remaining information gaps
- **Picking one code for mixed crew work.** Nadia confirmed days, not hours, and no splitting, but not the test that picks the single code. I use the code with the most days. Only Owen Petrakis is close (118 siding days against 97 roofing; 49,607.30 depends on it).
- **A clerical person who passes the five-day test at an employer with no field code** (Tomas Reyes, 64,212.48). Her rule has no code to move him to.
- **Things Nadia said she has no rule for.** None of these changes the six allocations:
  - an allowance paid with no travel days (Kyle Brandt, 390.00; she asked for a proposal, which is in the report);
  - a certificate in a slightly different name (Kent Island);
  - an owner who worked part of the year, or what amount applies to an owner who never does field work;
  - which source wins if the business description and payroll register disagree on the audit period.
- **Which payroll decides the field code with the most payroll** (employees only, or including subcontractor additions). This doesn't change any of the six.
- **Guide edition coverage.** Whether the July 2025 guide applies to the whole audit period is unknown; Nadia only knows the guide she has.

**On the last interview:** I don't think one is needed now. Most remaining gaps are cases Nadia already said she has no rule for, and she told us to propose, explain and flag them, which the report does. Only the mixed-crew test and Tomas Reyes could move dollars. I'd save the interview for Nadia's review of this first pass, or use it only if she disputes the "most days" choice.

## Not verified
- The interpretations above that Nadia hasn't confirmed.
- Whether the guide edition covers the full audit period.
- The "Employer's code" column in the report: the application names no one, so I paired people to its totals. It is used only to explain differences, never to classify.

## Verification and session evidence
- **What I ran:** the tests, a full run that fetches fresh from Drive, a single-employer run that produced the same CSV, the error paths, and hand recalculations for all changed totals.
- **What the validator checks:** the CSV format and `rationale_ref`, that totals and reconciliation match, that every cited record and rule exists, that every adjustment and open item is on the question list, and that no employer data is hard-coded.
- **Negative test:** I ran the validator on a deliberately broken copy, and it caught a changed cent, a fake rule label and a non-existent record file.
- **Session evidence:** each commit, including the final `b48e923`, carries an Entire checkpoint. The checkpoints are only local until you push.

file.content:
---
name: class-code-assistant
description: First-pass premium audit for Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation new business. It reads an employer's payroll register, application, business description, field notes and time records, then assigns company class codes. It allocates payroll to each code, citing the classification guide paragraph and the supporting records, and drafts employer-specific audit questions. Use it when a premium auditor asks to check, classify or allocate an employer's payroll, or to run the first pass on an employer file. It never sets rates or quotes premium.
---

# Class code assistant

This Skill does the first pass that Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, reviews before underwriting quotes an
employer. It classifies people and allocates payroll. It does **not** set rates, compute premium or quote.

## Ground rules

- **Use only the company's own rules.** The authoritative rules are the Linden Shore Mutual classification guide
  excerpt (paragraphs `CG-nn`), read from the location in `references/sources.json` on every run. Public
  classification manuals, such as NCCI or state manuals, do not apply and give wrong answers. Never use them.
- **Apply house practice as the auditor stated it.** `references/house-practice.md` keeps three lists apart:
  confirmed rules from interviews 1 and 2 (HP-1 to HP-15), stated gaps where the auditor has no rule, and the Skill's
  own readings (R2, R3, R4, R6, R14), which are always raised as open items. The numbers are in `references/house_practice.json`.
- **Classify by actual duties, not titles (HP-1).** The records in the file decide, not the employer's application
  (HP-7).
- **Gray areas: propose, explain and flag, never invent.** When neither the guide nor house practice covers a case,
  propose a treatment, write down why, and add an open item that goes on the employer's question list and
  that the auditor reviews (HP-10). Never present a proposal as company
  rule.
- **Keep facts apart from assumptions.** Every fact cites the employer record it comes from. Every assumption is an
  open item.

## Inputs

Per employer, one folder named by its slug (for example `acme-roofing`) holding:

| File | Required | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `payroll-register.csv` (`employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`, optional `travel_days,travel_allowance_paid`) | yes | wages per person; out-of-town allowance |
| `application.md` (table of code, employees, payroll; employer's note) | yes | the employer's own split, for comparison |
| a `.md` stating `Audit period <Month D, YYYY> to <Month D, YYYY>` (usually `business-description.md`) | yes | audit period filter |
| `field-notes.md`, `business-description.md` | no | duties, owner status, subcontractors |
| `*timesheet*.csv` (`date,employee_id,work_type,hours`) | no | crew work by type, counted in days (HP-2, HP-13, R2) |
| `*sign*in*.csv` (`date,employee_id,site`) | no | clerical job-site days; five or more moves the whole pay to the governing code (HP-4) |
| `route-log.csv` (`date,driver_id,ride_along_id`) + `weekly-payroll.csv` (`week_start,week_end,employee_id,gross_pay`) | no | route split: pay weeks with two or more ride days go to T-610 (HP-2) |
| `subcontractor-payments.csv` (`date,subcontractor,work,invoice,amount_paid`) + `insurance-certificates.csv` (`subcontractor,certificate_no,coverage_from,coverage_to`) | no | uninsured subcontractors; a certificate must cover the whole audit period (HP-5) |
| `*receipts*.csv` (`month` + receipts columns named in the worksheet) | no | caterer test: F-720 only if off-site catering is 40% or more of gross receipts (HP-14) |

Other files are listed in the report as not used. Give the reason in the worksheet's `unused_records`.

Plus one **worksheet** per employer, `deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`, holding the analyst's judgments (step 3).

## How to run

From the repository root, with Python 3.10 or later and no other dependencies:

1. **Fetch and scaffold.** Run `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`. This
   downloads the guide and employer files into `.cache/sources/` and writes an empty worksheet listing every person,
   work type, subcontracted trade and receipts column that needs a decision.
2. **Read everything.** Read the guide (`.cache/sources/classification-guide.md`) and every file in
   `.cache/sources/employers/<slug>/`. Note which statements are documented, and where the employer's application
   disagrees with its own records.
3. **Fill in the worksheet** following `references/worksheet.md`. For each person, record the code that describes
   what they actually do, a `basis` citing the record, and the `records` relied on. Map each timesheet work type, job
   subcontracted trade to a guide code, and name the off-site catering receipts columns. Record owners,
   documented facts, confirmations to ask the employer for, and open items for gray areas. Do **not** do arithmetic
   here; the engine applies the house rules.
4. **Run.** Use `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer <slug>` for one employer, or `--all`
   for every employer folder at the source. Add `--local <dir>` to use a local copy laid out as
   `<dir>/classification-guide.md` and `<dir>/employers/<slug>/`, instead of fetching.
5. **Check.** Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` and
   `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/validate.py`. Then read the report section and the questions as the
   auditor would, and fix the worksheet, not the outputs, if anything is wrong.
6. **Hand over** to the auditor for review (HP-11). The output is a first pass, not audit work.

## Outputs

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv` | Exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`. One row per code carrying payroll, dollars to the cent, `rationale_ref` = the guide paragraph describing the code |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` (`--all`) or `deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-report.md` | Call-first order with reasons. # Employer worksheet (`deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`)

The worksheet holds the judgments that need a reader: what each person actually does, and which guide code describes a
type of work. The engine does everything else from the records: the thresholds, splits, flat amounts, caps,
subcontractor shares and comparison with the employer. Start from `run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`.

Every code must be one the guide describes. Every judgment cites the record it rests on. If a record does not settle a
judgment, make the best-supported proposal and add an `open_items` entry; do not leave it implied.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `employees.<id>.duty_code` | The code describing the person's **actual** duties from the file (HP-1). For crew with timesheets, give the expected code; the timesheets then decide by days (HP-13, R2). For office staff, give `C-110`; the engine applies the five-day sign-in test and moves the person to the governing code (HP-4). For a catering crew member, give the caterer code; the engine applies the 40% receipts test (HP-14). |
| `employees.<id>.basis` | One or two sentences: what the person does, the record and date that show it, and the guide paragraph. Say so when the only evidence is a job title. |
| `employees.<id>.records` | Files the basis rests on. The payroll register is added automatically. |
| `owners.<id or name>` | `included` (no election of exclusion), `field_work`, `field_code` (the employer's trade code, HP-3), `basis`, `records`. Excluded owners are listed for the record only. |
| `work_type_codes` | Timesheet `work_type` to code. |
| `route_code` | Code for driver payroll in route ride-along weeks, when a route log exists (T-610, HP-2). |
| `receipts` | `{file, offsite_columns, other_columns}`: the gross receipts record and which columns are off-site catering, for the HP-14 test. |
| `subcontract_work_codes` | Subcontracted `work` to code. |
| `subcontractor_certificate_matches` | Payee name to certificate name, when they differ. Always raised as an open item. |
| `facts` | `{fact, record}` statements the report lists as documented. |
| `confirmations` | `{about, question}` employer questions for records relied on that the engine does not know about, such as an owner's exclusion election. Name the person or record and the document needed. |
| `open_items` | `{about, proposal, why, records, employer_question?, merge_with?}`. `merge_with` adds context to an item the engine raises for the same person. |
| `unused_records` | File name to the reason it was not used. |

"""Write the deliverables: one codes CSV per employer, the audit report and the employer question list.""" import csv from decimal import Decimal from .rules import fmt ZERO = Decimal("0.00") def write_codes_csv(path, result, guide): path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: w = csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n") w.writerow(["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]) for code, amount in result.totals.items(): if amount: w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", guide.ref_for(code)]) def change(result): """Payroll the first pass places in a code above what the employer reported there: moved in from another code or added (sum of positive per-code differences). Payroll dollars only; no rates involved.""" return sum((d for d in result.differences().values() if d > 0), ZERO) def call_order(results): return sorted(results, key=lambda r: (-change(r), -len(r.open_items), r.rec["employer_name"])) def _cell(text): return str(text).replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ") def _signed(d): return f"+{fmt(d)}" if d > 0 else fmt(d) def _drivers(result, n=3): big = sorted(result.adjustments, key=lambda a: -abs(a.amount))[:n] return "; ".join(f"{a.about}: {a.kind.lower()} ({fmt(a.amount)} under {a.code})" for a in big) def report(results, guide, run): out = ["# Premium audit first pass: class codes and payroll allocation", ""] out += [ "Prepared by the class-code-assistant Skill as a **first pass for review by Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium " "Auditor**. It is not audit work until she has reviewed it (house practice HP-11). It classifies and " "allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium.", "", f"- Classification rules: Linden Shore Mutual classification guide excerpt, edition of {guide.edition}, " f"sha256 `{run['guide_sha256'][:12]}`, read from {run['guide_source']}.", f"- Employer files read from {run['employer_source']} at {run['fetched_at']}.", "- Three kinds of statement are kept apart:", " - **Confirmed rules** (`HP-n`) are what Nadia Brennan stated in interviews 1 and 2, listed with timestamps " "in `skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md`, together with the guide (`CG-nn`).", " - **Facts** cite the employer record they come from.", " - **Open items** are unresolved judgements. Each one gives the proposed handling, why, and the Skill's " "reading (`R-n`) where one was needed. Each is on the employer's question list for confirmation, and Nadia " "reviews the proposal (HP-10).", "- **Questionable records** are used as written and sent to the employer to confirm (HP-15).", "", "## Which two employers to call first", "", "Nadia left the choice to the analyst, with reasons (HP-12). The order ranks employers by the payroll the " "first pass places in a code above what the employer reported there: payroll moved in from another code, plus " "payroll added. It is in dollars of payroll, not premium. A larger figure means the employer's own split, and " "so the figures underwriting would otherwise quote from, is further from the records. Ties go to the employer " "with more open items.", "", "| Order | Employer | Payroll placed differently | Net change | Employer reported | First pass | Open items | Employer questions |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|", ] ordered = call_order(results) for i, r in enumerate(ordered, 1): out.append(f"| {i} | {r.rec['employer_name']} | {fmt(change(r))} | " f"{_signed(sum(r.differences().values(), ZERO)) if any(r.differences().values()) else '0.00'} | " f"{fmt(sum(r.employer_split.values(), ZERO))} | {fmt(sum(r.totals.values(), ZERO))} | " f"{len(r.open_items)} | {len(r.questions)} |") out.append("") for i, r in enumerate(ordered[:2], 1): out.append(f"{i}. **{r.rec['employer_name']}**: {fmt(change(r))} of payroll is placed differently from the " f"employer's split. The largest drivers are {_drivers(r)}. Open items for the employer: " + ("; ".join(o.about for o in r.open_items) or "none") + ".") if len(ordered) > 2 and change(ordered[1]) and change(ordered[1]) - change(ordered[2]) <= change(ordered[1]) / 20: second, third = ordered[1], ordered[2] out += ["", f"Close call for second place: {third.rec['employer_name']} ({fmt(change(third))}) is within 5% of " f"{second.rec['employer_name']} ({fmt(change(second))}). Of the {fmt(change(third))}, " f"{fmt(sum((a.amount for a in third.adjustments if a.kind == 'Uninsured subcontractor payment added'), ZERO))} " f"is added only because certificates are missing from the file and could change if the employer " f"produces them. Nadia may prefer that call."] out += ["", "## Summary", "", "| Employer | Employer's split | Decision rests on |", "|---|---|---|"] for r in results: out.append(f"| {r.rec['employer_name']} | {'Accepted' if r.accepts_employer_split else 'Not accepted'} | " f"{_cell(_decision_records(r))} |") for r in results: out += [""] + _employer_section(r, guide) return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n" def _decision_records(r): recs = [] for p in r.people: recs += p.records for a in r.adjustments: recs += a.records return ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(x.split(" (")[0] for x in recs)) def _employer_section(r, guide): rec, ws = r.rec, r.ws start, end = rec["period"] out = [f"## {rec['employer_name']}", ""] out += [ f"Application {rec['application_id']}, signed by {rec['signed_by']}. Audit period {start.isoformat()} to " f"{end.isoformat()} ({rec['period_file']}). Files read: {', '.join(sorted(rec['file'].read))}.", "", ] if rec["employer_note"]: out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{rec['employer_note']}\"", ""] if r.accepts_employer_split: out += [f"**Employer's split: accepted.** The records give the same codes and payroll, to the cent, as the " f"employer reported. The decision rests on {_decision_records(r)}. Open items below still need " f"confirmation.", ""] else: out += [f"**Employer's split: not accepted.** The records in the file decide the allocation (HP-7). The " f"decision rests on {_decision_records(r)}. Each difference is on this employer's question list.", ""] out += ["### Allocation", "", "| Class code | Guide paragraph | Employer reported | First pass | Difference |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"] for code, d in r.differences().items(): out.append(f"| {code} | {guide.ref_for(code)} | {fmt(r.employer_split.get(code, ZERO))} | " f"{fmt(r.totals.get(code, ZERO))} | {_signed(d) if d else '0.00'} |") tot_e, tot_f = sum(r.employer_split.values(), ZERO), sum(r.totals.values(), ZERO) out += [f"| **Total** | | **{fmt(tot_e)}** | **{fmt(tot_f)}** | **{_signed(tot_f - tot_e) if tot_f != tot_e else '0.00'}** |", ""] out += [f"Confirmed rules that decided or changed something here: {', '.join(sorted(r.applied, key=lambda x: int(x[3:]))) or 'HP-1, HP-7 only'}. " f"Governing code (field code carrying the most payroll, HP-4): {r.governing_code or 'none, no field code'}.", ""] out += ["Reconciliation:", "", "| Step | Amount (USD) |", "|---|---|"] out += [f"| {_cell(label)} | {_signed(v) if i and i < len(r.reconciliation) - 1 else fmt(v)} |" for i, (label, v) in enumerate(r.reconciliation)] + [""] out += ["### Where and why the first pass differs from the employer's split", ""] if not r.adjustments: out += ["No difference. No adjustment was needed.", ""] else: for code, d in r.differences().items(): if not d: continue into = [f"{a.about} ({a.kind.lower()}, {fmt(a.amount)})" for a in r.adjustments if a.code == code] out_of = [f"{p.name} ({fmt(p.wages)} reported here, now " + ", ".join(f"{fmt(l.amount)} {l.code}" for l in p.lines) + ")" for p in r.people if p.employer_code == code and {l.code for l in p.lines} != {code}] parts = (["in: " + "; ".join(into)] if into else []) + (["out: " + "; ".join(out_of)] if out_of else []) out.append(f"- **{code}** {_signed(d)}: " + (". ".join(parts) or "see the adjustments below") + ".") out.append(f"- How the employer's split was compared: {r.inference}.") out.append("") out += ["### Adjustments", "", "| # | Employee or payment | Adjustment | Amount (USD) | Code | Detail | Records | Rule |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"] for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1): out.append(f"| {i} | {_cell(a.about)} | {a.kind} | {fmt(a.amount)} | {a.code} | {_cell(a.detail)} | " f"{_cell(', '.join(a.records))} | {a.rule} |") out.append("") out += ["### Employee by employee", "", "| ID | Name | Position | Register wages | Employer's code (paired from application totals) | First pass | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"] for p in r.people: alloc = "
".join(f"{fmt(l.amount)} {l.code}" for l in p.lines) basis = "

"""Check the deliverables against the assignment's format rules. Exit status 1 on any failure.

Checks: the six codes CSVs (exact header, cents, no zero rows, rationale_ref as printed in the guide); CSV totals match
the report's allocation tables; one report and one question section per employer; every adjustment in the report is
named in that employer's questions; no employer names or IDs are hard-coded in the Skill's code; interview exports
are unchanged since they were committed.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402

HEADER = ["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]
CENTS = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d{2}$")


def sections(text):
    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", text, flags=re.M)
    return {parts[i].strip(): parts[i + 1] for i in range(1, len(parts), 2)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="deliverables", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--guide", default=".cache/sources/classification-guide.md", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--employers", default=".cache/sources/employers", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    failures, checks = [], 0

    def check(ok, message):
        nonlocal checks
        checks += 1
        if not ok:
            failures.append(message)

    guide = Guide(args.guide.read_text())
    house_practice = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "references" / "house-practice.md").read_text()
    slugs = sorted(p.name for p in args.employers.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
    report = (args.out / "audit-report.md").read_text()
    questions = (args.out / "audit-questions.md").read_text()
    rep_sections, q_sections = sections(report), sections(questions)
    names = {}

    for slug in slugs:
        app = (args.employers / slug / "application.md").read_text()
        name = re.search(r"^#\s*([^:\n]+)", app, re.M).group(1).strip()
        names[slug] = name
        path = args.out / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv"
        check(path.exists(), f"{path} is missing")
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        with open(path, newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
        check(rows and rows[0] == HEADER, f"{path}: header must be exactly {','.join(HEADER)}")
        body = rows[1:]
        check(len({r[0] for r in body}) == len(body), f"{path}: a class code appears more than once")
        totals = {}
        for r in body:
            check(len(r) == 3, f"{path}: row {r} does not have 3 columns")
            code, amount, ref = r
            check(CENTS.match(amount) is not None, f"{path}: {amount!r} is not dollars to the cent without separators")
            check(Decimal(amount) > 0, f"{path}: {code} has zero payroll")
            check(guide.code_ref.get(code) == ref, f"{path}: {code} rationale_ref {ref!r} is not the guide paragraph "
                                                   f"{guide.code_ref.get(code)!r}")
            totals[code] = Decimal(amount)

        sec = rep_sections.get(name)
        check(sec is not None, f"audit-report.md has no section '## {name}'")
        check(name in q_sections, f"audit-questions.md has no section '## {name}'")
        if sec is None:
            continue
        table = {m[0]: Decimal(m[2].replace(",", "")) for m in
                 re.findall(r"^\| ([A-Z]-\d{3}) \| (CG-\d+) \| [\d,.]+ \| ([\d,.]+) \|", sec, re.M)}
        table = {c: v for c, v in table.items() if v}
        check(table == totals, f"{name}: CSV totals {totals} differ from the report's allocation table {table}")
        adj = re.search(r"### Adjustments\n\n(.*?)\n\n", sec, re.S)
        qtext = q_sections.get(name, "")
        for row in (adj.group(1).splitlines()[2:] if adj else []):
            about = row.split(" | ")[1].split(", invoice")[0]
            check(about in qtext, f"{name}: adjustment about {about!r} has no question naming it")
        check("Employer's split: accepted" in sec or "Employer's split: not accepted" in sec,
              f"{name}: the report does not state whether the employer's split is accepted")

        recon = re.search(r"\| First-pass total \(equals the sum of the codes CSV\) \| ([\d,.]+) \|", sec)
        check(recon is not None and Decimal(recon.group(1).replace(",", "")) == sum(totals.values(), Decimal(0)),
              f"{name}: reconciliation total missing or differs from the CSV total {sum(totals.values(), Decimal(0))}")

        folder = {p.name for p in (args.employers / slug).iterdir()}
        for cited in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\b([a-z][a-z0-9-]*\.(?:csv|md))\b", sec))):
            check(cited in folder, f"{name}: cites record {cited}, which is not in the employer file")
        for ref in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bCG-\d+\b", sec))):
            check(ref in guide.paragraphs, f"{name}: cites {ref}, which is not a paragraph in the guide")
        for ref in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\b(HP-\d+|R\d+)\b", sec))):
            check(re.search(rf"\b{ref}\b", house_practice) is not None,
                  f"{name}: cites {ref}, which is not defined in house-practice.md")

        items = re.search(r"### Open items: unresolved judgements\n\n.*?\n\n(.*?)\n\n", sec, re.S)
        check(items is not None, f"{name}: no open items section")
        for row in (items.group(1).splitlines()[2:] if items and items.group(1).startswith("|") else []):
            about = row.split(" | ")[1]
            check(f"**{about}.**" in qtext or about in qtext, f"{name}: open item {about!r} is not on the question list")

    check(re.search(r"\brate[sd]? (of|at) \d|premium (of|is) \$?\d", report, re.I) is None,
          "audit-report.md appears to state a rate or premium figure")

    skill_code = "\n".join(p.read_text() for p in Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.rglob("*") if p.suffix in {".py", ".json", ".md"})
    for slug, name in names.items():
        check(slug not in skill_code and name not in skill_code, f"the Skill's code or references mention {name}")
    for slug in slugs:
        with open(args.employers / slug / "payroll-register.csv", newline="") as f:
            for r in csv.DictReader(f):
                check(r["employee_id"] not in skill_code and r["name"] not in skill_code,
                      f"the Skill's code or references mention {r['employee_id']} {r['name']}")

    changed = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD", "--", "interviews"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    check(changed.returncode == 0 and not changed.stdout.strip(), f"interview exports changed since commit: {changed.stdout}")
    tracked = set(subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "interviews"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split())
    on_disk = {f"interviews/{p.name}" for p in Path("interviews").glob("*.md")}
    check(on_disk and on_disk <= tracked, f"interview exports not committed: {sorted(on_disk - tracked)}")
    for f in sorted(tracked):
        history = subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--format=%h", "--", f], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
        check(len(history) == 1, f"{f} was changed after it was first committed ({len(history)} commits touch it)")

    for f in failures:
        print(f"FAIL {f}")
    print(f"{checks - len(failures)}/{checks} checks passed")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- supabase: Use when doing ANY task involving Supabase. Triggers: Supabase products (Database, Auth, Edge Functions, Realtime, Storage, Vectors, Cron, Queues); client libraries and SSR integrations (supabase-js, @supabase/ssr) in Next.js, React, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix; auth issues (login, logout, sessions, JWT, cookies, getSession, getUser, getClaims, RLS); Supabase CLI or MCP server; schema changes, migrations, declarative schemas, security audits, Postgres extensions (pg_graphql, pg_cron, pg_vector); debugging and troubleshooting errors or unexpected behavior on Supabase projects (HTTP errors, Postgres errors, RLS surprises, permission denied, schema cache issues, timeouts, Edge Function crashes, Realtime drops, Storage failures) and reading or querying logs (Logs Explorer, ClickHouse).
- supabase-postgres-best-practices: Postgres best practices maintained by Supabase, for Postgres running anywhere. Load this skill BEFORE writing or changing anything that lives in a Postgres database: creating or altering tables and columns (including choosing column types), schema design, migrations and declarative schema files, RLS policies and the tests that verify them, indexes, triggers, database functions, queues and scheduled jobs (pg_cron, pgmq), vector/semantic search (pgvector), and restoring dumps (pg_restore) or importing data. Also load it when diagnosing slow queries, high CPU, timeouts, EXPLAIN plans, connection exhaustion, locking, bloat, or rows visible to the wrong user or tenant. This is not just a performance guide — schema, migration, security, and SQL authoring tasks need these rules too, even for a one-column change or a single query.
- apprentice-workspace:choose-automation-approach: Guide an adaptive interview to choose proportionate deployment, integration, credential, and high-stakes controls when designing or revisiting an automated workflow.
- apprentice-workspace:command-failed: A command, install or setup step failed and you are not sure what to do with it. Use when the user says it did not work, it is broken, I got an error, I am stuck, 跑不起來, 壞掉了, 卡住了, or pastes an error they have not explained. Also use when a setup step has been retried more than once without changing anything.
- apprentice-workspace:create-skill: Scaffold new Claude Code skill following architecture principles (three-tier disclosure, gotchas, eval). Use when user asks to create, build, or author a new skill or SKILL.md.
- apprentice-workspace:diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- apprentice-workspace:digest-doc: Digest a document the business already has into a page-sourced fact-sheet. One family: article - anything written down, from a supplier agreement to a printed procedure to a web page. Use on digest this, summarize this document, or a document the owner hands you.
- apprentice-workspace:drive-portal: Use when driving a legacy or government web form through the Chrome extension — popup uploads, nested framesets, derived hidden fields, or a save that fails with an error naming nothing.
- apprentice-workspace:explain: Use when the reader is unfamiliar with a field and needs to reach competence, not merely asking how something works. Applies the explanation register; explanation and digest stay separate.
- apprentice-workspace:flowchart: Build a flowchart, system map or process diagram as validated inline SVG - ISO 5807 symbols, automatic layered placement, four self-tested checks. Use whenever a document needs a diagram.
- apprentice-workspace:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- apprentice-workspace:interview-recording: Use when an interview recording must become a session record: transcribe with speaker labels, refine, reduce to key points, decisions, open questions. Fires on transcribe this interview.
- apprentice-workspace:kb-restructure: Rename, move, re-nest, or ARCHIVE a KB file/dir without breaking inbound refs — discover, classify live-vs-historical, execute, fix, verify (split/merge staged). Fire on any structural mutation ask.
- apprentice-workspace:onboarding: Walk a new AI Fellowship apprentice from a fresh machine to a working workspace, verifying each step that a command can verify and recording the ones only they can confirm. Use on an apprentice's first session, and again on any later session while the record still shows unfinished items. Do not use it to set up a client engagement — that is playbook-environment-setup.md, which assumes everything this skill installs.
- apprentice-workspace:scan-agent-skill: Scan a local agent skill package for prompt injection, data exfiltration, malicious code, obfuscation, and risky tool use with a pinned security scanner. Use before installing or executing a third-party skill, after modifying a skill, or before handing a skill over. Do not use a clean scan as proof that a skill is safe.
- apprentice-workspace:setup: Set up the apprentice workspace folder, with its rules, in the repository you are working in. Use once in each new repository, or when apprentice-workspace/ is missing or incomplete.
- apprentice-workspace:video-to-markdown: Turn a screen recording into one markdown file — the full transcript as the spine, screenshots interleaved at the moment each screen was on display. Use on a screen recording of someone doing their work, a walkthrough, a demo, plus an optional audio-only continuation file.
- apprentice-workspace:workspace-help: Answer an apprentice's "how do I ...?" and "where does this go?" questions about this workspace by listing what is actually in it right now and reading its manifests, never from a remembered inventory. Use whenever someone asks which skills they have, where a file belongs, what a playbook or skill is for, what they are allowed to edit, or which tool to reach for. Do not use it to run a playbook or to set anything up.
- apprentice-workspace:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
- apprentice-workspace:youtube-transcript: Turn a video URL into a clean markdown transcript — free captions when the video carries them, a local transcription pass when it does not. Triggers on youtube transcript, transcribe this video, get the text of that walkthrough.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo).
